1#_: It was mixed with others. See in responsa at the end of his Shabbat siddur responsum 3, where he was uncertain about something that has a permitted aspect that was mixed, and afterward one of them explained whether we say "everything that separated," etc. — that it is not relevant to say "until you eat it in prohibition eat it after Yom Tov in permission," for we presume there is no prohibition at all; or we do not say at all regarding something that has a permitted aspect that we follow the majority even in such a case — and he elaborated on this; and in the end he concluded that even in such a case we do not say "everything that separated," etc.; and this is also within the rule of something that has a permitted aspect; and so is implied in responsa of Tzemach Tzedek siman 69 in the middle of the responsum — see there; and so wrote Magen Avraham in siman 513 s.k. 13; and see in Tzelach on Beitzah 4 Yom Tov 2b s.v. "and since he elaborated to bring proof that we say regarding something that has a permitted aspect 'everything that separated returns to the majority'" — see there; and so appears to be the opinion of Chavot Yair in siman 233 — see there.
2#_: It was mixed not in its kind. See in responsa of Radbaz part 2 siman 217.
3#_: There are those who say. See Shach; and see in responsa Zichron Yosef Yoreh Deah siman 26; and see what my uncle the great rabbi R' Elazar, may his memory be blessed, wrote in Chemdat Yamim discourse 6; and in responsa Keter Kehunah siman 45; and in responsa Toldot Yitzchak siman 23; and see in the novellae of the Gaon R' Yonatan, may his memory be blessed, on Laws of Yom Tov of Rambam chapter 2 law 1; and in Bnei Chayya what he wrote on this; and see further in Shaar HaMelech chapter 8 of Laws of Forbidden Foods rule 11 what he wrote on this.
4#_: Will certainly come in any event. See in responsa Tzemach Tzedek siman 69 on a doubtful tereifah egg laid on Yom Tov that was mixed — the questioner ruled it is not something that has a permitted aspect, since even after Yom Tov there will be no permission without nullification on account of tereifah; and he, may his memory be blessed, disagrees, for nevertheless it will certainly come to permission somewhat, for after Yom Tov the inclusive prohibition of being born will be removed and everything possible to do in permission we do — see there; and so agreed Peri Chadash and Menachem Tziyon general rule 74 sign 12; and see Peri Megadim who wrote similarly regarding one who said "konam on me eating this nevelah" and it was mixed — vow prohibition is in any case something that has a permitted aspect and is not nullified even in sixty; one can say vow prohibition does not apply at all since it is not in a mixture — nevertheless there are two prohibitions, only that there is not one prohibition from two sources, meaning to receive two sets of lashes or two sins; or it is called something that has a permitted aspect — see there; and see in responsa of Rabbeinu Akiva Eiger siman 65 who was asked on this law and initially also wanted to say that nevertheless vow prohibition is something that has a permitted aspect; however not for Peri Megadim's reason but since there is a dispute of the rabbis whether a vow takes effect on something already forbidden (see below siman 276 seif 5) — its doubt is stringent — if so it is something that has a permitted aspect; and he again questioned this, for nevertheless there is room to permit in our case, since that vows are something that has a permitted aspect is explained in the Gemara because there is a mitzvah to ask — if so in our case it is obvious there is no mitzvah, etc. — see the full responsum.
